# Shopware Storefront — where template variables come from

A template reads only what something put in scope. Four sources do that, and knowing which one supplies a variable decides whether an override works in every context or only in the one you tested.

**8 global variables from 25 Twig extensions, 45 templates receiving controller variables, 218 include hand-offs, 915 local assignments.**

## Contents

- [The four sources](#the-four-sources)
- [Global variables and where they come from](#global-variables-and-where-they-come-from)
- [Functions and filters, and which extension provides them](#functions-and-filters-and-which-extension-provides-them)
- [Variables a controller passes](#variables-a-controller-passes)
- [Variables passed between templates](#variables-passed-between-templates)
- [Variables a template defines itself](#variables-a-template-defines-itself)

## The four sources

1. **Global** — added by a Twig extension to every template. Always available, including in a partial reached through several includes.
2. **Controller** — the array handed to `renderStorefront()`. Almost always just `page`, which carries everything else on the page struct.
3. **Include** — `sw_include ... with {...}` puts named values in the included template's scope. Without `only`, the including scope stays visible too, which is why a partial can silently depend on a variable nobody passed it.
4. **Local** — `{% set %}` and the loop variable of `{% for %}`, visible from that point to the end of the enclosing block.

**The trap when overriding.** A `{% set %}` in a parent block is not visible to a child block you override in your own template: blocks resolve in their own scope. Re-derive the value, or override the block that holds the `{% set %}` instead.

## Global variables and where they come from

`Storefront/Framework/Twig/TemplateDataExtension.php` implements `GlobalsInterface` and its `getGlobals()` runs once per request, reading the current request from the `RequestStack`.

**It returns an empty array when there is no current request, or when the request carries no `SalesChannelContext`.** So in a context outside a sales channel — a rendered mail template, a generated document — none of these exist. Guard with `{% if context is defined %}` in a template that both paths reach.

| Variable | Carries |
|---|---|
| `activeRoute` | the matched route name; navigation templates compare against it |
| `context` | the `SalesChannelContext`: customer, currency, tax state, payment and shipping method |
| `controllerAction` | the method that handled the request, e.g. `index` |
| `controllerName` | the controller without its suffix, e.g. `Product` — used for body classes |
| `formViolations` | validation errors of the previous request, for re-rendering a failed form |
| `jsonLdFlags` | the `json_encode` flags used for structured data output |
| `shopware` | config bag: `dateFormat`, `navigation` (active and root id), `minSearchLength`, `showStagingBanner` |
| `themeId` | id of the resolved theme; read by `theme_config()` rather than directly |

The navigation ids inside `shopware.navigation` are resolved in a fixed order: the route's `navigationId` attribute first, then the request parameter, then the category of a landing page, and finally the sales channel's root category. That is why a landing page still highlights the right navigation entry.

## Functions and filters, and which extension provides them

Not variables, but the other half of what a template can reach. Each is registered by one extension class; the path says whether it comes from the core or the Storefront.

| Extension | Functions | Filters |
|---|---|---|
| `BackwardCompatibleIntlExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/BackwardCompatibleIntlExtension.php`</sub> | — | `format_*_number`, `format_currency`, `format_number` |
| `BuildBreadcrumbExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/BuildBreadcrumbExtension.php`</sub> | `sw_breadcrumb_full()`, `sw_breadcrumb_full_by_id()` | — |
| `CategoryUrlExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/CategoryUrlExtension.php`</sub> | `category_linknewtab()`, `category_url()` | — |
| `ComparisonExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/ComparisonExtension.php`</sub> | `compare()` | — |
| `ConfigExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/ConfigExtension.php`</sub> | `config()` | — |
| `ConfigExtension`<br><sub>`storefront/Framework/Twig/Extension/ConfigExtension.php`</sub> | `import_map()`, `theme_config()`, `theme_css_vars()`, `theme_scripts()` | — |
| `CurrencyFilter`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Filter/CurrencyFilter.php`</sub> | — | `currency` |
| `DoctrineExtension`<br><sub>`core/Profiling/Twig/DoctrineExtension.php`</sub> | — | `doctrine_format_sql`, `doctrine_prettify_sql`, `doctrine_replace_query_parameters` |
| `EmailIdnTwigFilter`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Filter/EmailIdnTwigFilter.php`</sub> | — | `decodeIdnEmail`, `encodeIdnEmail` |
| `FeatureFlagExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/FeatureFlagExtension.php`</sub> | `feature()`, `getAllFeatures()` | — |
| `IconCacheTwigFilter`<br><sub>`storefront/Framework/Twig/Extension/IconCacheTwigFilter.php`</sub> | `sw_icon_cache_disable()`, `sw_icon_cache_enable()` | `sw_icon_cache` |
| `InAppPurchaseExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/InAppPurchaseExtension.php`</sub> | `allInAppPurchases()`, `inAppPurchase()` | — |
| `LeadingSpacesFilter`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Filter/LeadingSpacesFilter.php`</sub> | — | `remove_leading_spaces` |
| `MeasurementConvertUnitTwigFilter`<br><sub>`core/Content/MeasurementSystem/TwigExtension/MeasurementConvertUnitTwigFilter.php`</sub> | — | `sw_convert_unit` |
| `MediaExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/MediaExtension.php`</sub> | `searchMedia()` | — |
| `PcreExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/PcreExtension.php`</sub> | `preg_match()` | `preg_replace` |
| `PhpSyntaxExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/PhpSyntaxExtension.php`</sub> | `array()`, `version_compare()` | `boolval`, `floatval`, `intval`, `json_encode`, `md5`, `sha256`, `strval` |
| `RawUrlFunctionExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/RawUrlFunctionExtension.php`</sub> | `rawUrl()` | — |
| `ReplaceRecursiveFilter`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Filter/ReplaceRecursiveFilter.php`</sub> | — | `replace_recursive` |
| `SecurityExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/SecurityExtension.php`</sub> | — | `filter`, `find`, `map`, `reduce`, `sort` |
| `SeoUrlFunctionExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/SeoUrlFunctionExtension.php`</sub> | `seoUrl()` | — |
| `SwSanitizeTwigFilter`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/SwSanitizeTwigFilter.php`</sub> | — | `sw_sanitize` |
| `TwigFeaturesWithInheritanceExtension`<br><sub>`core/Framework/Adapter/Twig/Extension/TwigFeaturesWithInheritanceExtension.php`</sub> | `sw_block()`, `sw_include()`, `sw_source()` | — |
| `UrlEncodingTwigFilter`<br><sub>`storefront/Framework/Twig/Extension/UrlEncodingTwigFilter.php`</sub> | — | `sw_encode_media_url`, `sw_encode_url` |
| `ZugferdTwigExtension`<br><sub>`core/Checkout/DocumentV2/Template/ZugferdTwigExtension.php`</sub> | — | `zugferd_date_102`, `zugferd_decimal` |

`sw_extends`, `sw_include`, `sw_block` and `sw_source` come from `TwigFeaturesWithInheritanceExtension`: they are the multi-inheritance aware replacements for Twig's own tags, which is why a plugin template can extend a template another plugin already extended.

## Variables a template defines itself

`{% set %}` assignments and `{% for %}` loop variables, per template. A block you override cannot see these unless it sits inside the block that defines them.

- `storefront/base.html.twig` — sets `isHMRMode`, `options`; loops `messages`, `type`
- `storefront/block/cms-block-app-renderer.html.twig` — sets `appTwigBlockName`, `element`; loops `slot`
- `storefront/block/cms-block-category-heading.html.twig` — sets `element`
